title: Translating a poem
bodyMd: A translator preserves a poem’s repeated sounds in one passage but changes its word order. A reviewer objects that the translation is not literal. The translator agrees, explaining that retaining every original word order would destroy the repeated sounds in the new language. She offers notes explaining where she chose sound over syntax, without claiming that this is the only defensible translation.
